Subject: Private deployment capacity proposal & mutual action plan

Hi Priya / Acme team —

Following our workshop last week, attached is the initial proforma for the private GPU pool we discussed plus a short network checklist. High-level asks from our side: confirm the target steady-state throughput, the pilot window for validation, and the primary contact for network/VLAN provisioning.

Key assumptions in the proforma (page 1):
- Target 95th pctl throughput: 12k tokens/sec sustained (avg request ~40 tokens)
- Expected peak burst: 3x sustained for up to 5 minutes
- Latency SLO: 95th pctl < 300ms for sync generation at 512 token truncation
- Default headroom: 30% reserved capacity per tenant to absorb microbursts

Attachments: PrivPool-Proforma-202605.pdf, Network-Checklist.xlsx

Suggested next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Acme confirms throughput target and pilot scope (this thread) — by Tue 5/26
2) Redwood provides final config and onboarding runbook — target Thu 5/28
3) Pilot (2 weeks) — target start Mon 6/7

If those dates look good, we can send the DocuSign proforma with the pilot addendum.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the draft. A couple of quick clarifying questions from the infra team at Acme and my side as the implementation consultant:
- The proforma mentions 30% headroom per tenant. Is that additive to cluster-level spare capacity, or is it the same buffer? In other words, what is the total soft reserve we need to provision on the NIC/cluster?
- NIC oversubscription: do you plan to rely on NIC oversubscribe (1.5x) for burst absorption, or do you expect cross-node migration for bursts?

If you can drop a short table with the expected sustained, expected peak, and recommended NIC provisioning per GPU node, that will help procurement size the network links.

Cheers,
Rajiv
EdgeCloud — Senior Deployment Architect

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Kumar <rajiv@edgecloud.io>, AcmeCorp Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment capacity proposal & mutual action plan

Rajiv — great questions. Quick answers inline and a short table below.

- Headroom: the 30% callout is tenant-level soft reserve that sits inside the cluster carveout for Acme. In practice we recommend an additional cluster-level spare pool of ~15% for maintenance and cross-tenant failover — so cumulative effective spare is ~43% when you combine both (note: we do not double-count identical capacity; this is a conservative sizing approach).
- NIC oversubscription: we generally avoid heavy NIC oversubscribe for private deployments where egress cost and predictability matter. Recommended baseline is 1.1x NIC provisioning to allow for transient bursts; we rely on cross-node request routing + KV/prefix caching to smooth bursts beyond that.

Quick sizing table (recommended):
- Sustained throughput: 12k tokens/sec (~300 reqs/sec at 40 tokens)
- Peak burst (design): 36k tokens/sec (3x sustained) for up to 5 minutes
- GPU node: 4x A100-equivalent per pod, baseline NIC: 100Gbps per node (1.1x oversubscribe allowed)
- Cluster pool: initial carveout 10 pods (40 GPUs) + 15% cluster spare = effective 46 GPUs

Operational notes:
- Autoscale cadence: 5 min evaluation windows, scale step of 1 pod, warm-pool minimum of 2 pods to keep KV caches warm.
- Fallback: streaming fall back to a smaller quantized model variant (Q4_8) if sustained latency degradation observed >3x SLO for 10 minutes.

I'll attach a quick network link recommendation and update the proforma if you want us to make the numbers explicit in the DocuSign.

Best,
Alex
